primitives.name: Phantom Image Persistence Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: When I first found myself doing this I used to think it was merely because I knew the lines imperfectly; but I have quite convinced myself that I really do see an image.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: I(t): Intensity of mental image at time t (arbitrary units), tau: Persistence decay constant (seconds)
primitives.assumptions: Mental imagery possesses a measurable persistence independent of external sensory input.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if the perceived image is purely hallucinatory without structural memory constraints, rendering tau undefined.

layer2.mapping: Models the GSE internal replay buffer where past game states are rendered visually, overriding immediate sensory inputs during high-load decision making.
layer2.telemetry: Latency between stimulus cessation and complete dissipation of internal visual representation.

Galton's empirical collection establishes a foundational dataset, transforming qualitative introspection into a quantifiable metric. For typical agents, P is weak or non-existent; however, for the boundary cases identified, P becomes the dominant processing channel. The text highlights a specific duality: the confusion between imperfect memory retrieval and genuine visual generation. Mathematically, this represents a phase transition in the cognitive state space. When the intensity of the internal image exceeds a critical threshold, the agent's decision-making architecture shifts from semantic processing to geometric/spatial manipulation. This is modeled as a bifurcation in the dynamical system governing attention allocation. The failure mode arises when the system attempts to apply linear interpolation between these distinct cognitive regimes. The 'ghost' mentioned in the text symbolizes the residual error term when a standard acoustic model attempts to fit a highly visual cognitive profile. By isolating the boundary cases, we extract the eigenfunctions of this visual processing operator. These eigenfunctions describe the maximal deviations in information encoding. In the context of sports intelligence, this translates to identifying agents who process complex tactical formations not as abstract rules, but as persistent, manipulable visual structures. The persistence kernel ensures that these structures remain stable under the high-frequency perturbations of live gameplay, allowing for rapid, intuitive state-transitions that bypass slower, deliberative reasoning pathways.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive traces its lineage to Francis Galton's late 19th-century inquiries into human faculty, specifically his pioneering work on the heritability of mental imagery. It bridges early empirical psychology with modern computational cognitive science. Historically, it challenged the prevailing assumption of uniform cognitive architecture, introducing the concept of phenotypic variation in sensory processing. This mathematical formalization resurrects those early observations, mapping them onto contemporary Bayesian frameworks for modeling heterogeneous agent capabilities in dynamic environments.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: We model opposing agents as possessing distinct latent parameters governing their reliance on visual versus semantic processing. An agent with high visual persistence may anticipate opponent movements by mentally projecting trajectories onto a spatial grid, effectively 'seeing' the future state. Conversely, an agent relying on semantic rules may struggle with novel, unscripted situations. Understanding this dichotomy allows our engine to predict decision latency and accuracy. If we identify an opponent operating primarily via the visual equivalent projection, we can exploit their potential blindness to non-spatial, abstract tactical feints.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A strict veto condition applies if the visual imagery reported is clinically pathological (e.g., severe hallucinations) rather than a benign variation of normal cognition. Our models assume the visual projections are structurally constrained by memory and reality. If the internal images lack fidelity to external physical laws, the isomorphism to GSE state-transition logic collapses. Furthermore, we veto any collinearity between visual vividness and general intelligence unless explicitly supported by the specific dataset, preventing spurious correlations from contaminating the predictive kernels.
